# Configuration reference

This page lists every cindermill configuration option with its type, accepted range, and the value it ships with. Options live in `cindermill.toml` under the table named for their subsystem.

## Cache table

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cache_dir | string | /var/cache/cindermill | Root directory for stored objects and index shards. |
| cache_ttl_hours | integer | 72 | Age at which an object that has not been read becomes eligible for eviction. |
| max_object_size_mib | integer | 2048 | Objects above this size are passed through to the backend without being cached. |
| evict_watermark_percent | integer | 85 | Used space above which the eviction sweep runs continuously instead of on a timer. |
| remote_verify | boolean | false | Re-hash objects after they are downloaded from a peer. |

## Network table

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| listen_port | integer | 7345 | TCP port the daemon binds on every interface. |
| peer_timeout_ms | integer | 1200 | Per-peer request timeout for object transfers. |
| max_peers | integer | 64 | Concurrent peer connections the daemon accepts. |

## Validation

`cindermill doctor` compares a local file against this reference and prints every option whose value differs from the shipped one. Ranges are enforced at load time; an out-of-range value stops the daemon rather than being clamped.

Last reviewed 2026-06-30.

web_fixture.content:
# cindermill

A content-addressed build cache for heterogeneous build fleets. cindermill sits between your compilers and object storage, deduplicating artefacts across machines and keeping hot objects on local NVMe.

- Content-addressed storage with automatic deduplication
- Peer-to-peer object transfer between fleet nodes
- Pluggable backends: S3, GCS, plain filesystem
- Single static binary; configuration in TOML

## Getting started

```
brew install cindermill
cindermill init --backend s3://northgate-buildcache
cindermill serve
```

## Documentation

The configuration reference on docs.cindermill.dev lists every option with its type and the value it ships with. Release notes live in CHANGELOG.md.

Apache-2.0. Maintained by the cindermill contributors.

web_fixture.content:
# Build-cache bakeoff: four daemons on a 200-core fleet

*Posted 2025-12-09 by Priya Raghunathan - Ironbridge HPC notes*

We put four build caches through the same monorepo: 41,000 targets, a cold cache, and a fleet of 200 build agents on a shared 25 GbE fabric.

## Results

| Daemon | Cold build | Warm build | Peak memory |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cindermill | 18m 40s | 2m 05s | 3.4 GiB |
| sandpiper | 21m 10s | 2m 55s | 5.1 GiB |
| brickvault | 23m 35s | 3m 20s | 4.2 GiB |
| drystone | 26m 50s | 4m 05s | 2.9 GiB |

## What we took away

cindermill recovered fastest after we fenced a rack mid-build, and its TOML file was the shortest to review line by line. None of that says much about how a daemon ships, though: every one of these tools starts conservative and wants tuning once the fleet is warm.

*Priya Raghunathan leads build infrastructure at Ironbridge HPC.*
